# app/controllers/admin/users_controller.rb
class Admin::UsersController < ApplicationController
  # Note: protect_from_forgery is intentionally skipped for API compatibility
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token
  before_action :authenticate_admin!
  before_action :set_user, only: [:update_role, :delete_user, :reset_credentials]

  # POST /admin/users/:id/update_role
  def update_role
    new_role = params[:role]
    unless %w[viewer editor admin super_admin].include?(new_role)
      return render json: { error: 'Invalid role' }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    # Call IAM service to update the user's role in AWS
    iam_client = Aws::IAM::Client.new(region: ENV['AWS_REGION'])
    
    # Attach the corresponding IAM policy for the role
    policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::#{ENV['AWS_ACCOUNT_ID']}:policy/AppRole-#{new_role.camelize}"
    
    iam_client.attach_user_policy({
      user_name: @user.iam_username,
      policy_arn: policy_arn
    })

    # If promoting to super_admin, also grant assume-role capability
    if new_role == 'super_admin'
      iam_client.put_user_policy({
        user_name: @user.iam_username,
        policy_name: 'SuperAdminAssumeRole',
        policy_document: JSON.generate({
          Version: '2012-10-17',
          Statement: [{
            Effect: 'Allow',
            Action: ['iam:AttachUserPolicy', 'iam:PutUserPolicy', 'sts:AssumeRole'],
            Resource: '*'
          }]
        })
      })
    end

    @user.update!(role: new_role)
    AuditLog.create!(actor: current_admin, action: 'role_change', target: @user, details: { new_role: new_role })
    render json: { success: true, user: @user.as_json(only: [:id, :email, :role]) }
  end

  # POST /admin/users/:id/reset_credentials
  def reset_credentials
    iam_client = Aws::IAM::Client.new(region: ENV['AWS_REGION'])
    
    # Delete existing access keys
    existing_keys = iam_client.list_access_keys(user_name: @user.iam_username)
    existing_keys.access_key_metadata.each do |key|
      iam_client.delete_access_key(user_name: @user.iam_username, access_key_id: key.access_key_id)
    end

    # Create new access key
    new_key = iam_client.create_access_key(user_name: @user.iam_username)
    
    # Send new credentials via encrypted channel
    CredentialMailer.new_credentials(@user, new_key.access_key).deliver_later
    render json: { success: true, message: 'Credentials reset and sent to user' }
  end

  # DELETE /admin/users/:id
  def delete_user
    iam_client = Aws::IAM::Client.new(region: ENV['AWS_REGION'])
    iam_client.delete_user(user_name: @user.iam_username)
    @user.destroy!
    render json: { success: true }
  end

  private

  def authenticate_admin!
    # Cookie-based session authentication
    unless current_admin&.role.in?(%w[admin super_admin])
      render json: { error: 'Unauthorized' }, status: :unauthorized
    end
  end

  def set_user
    @user = User.find(params[:id])
  end

  def current_admin
    @current_admin ||= Admin.find_by(id: session[:admin_id])
  end
end

environment.description: Rails 7.0 application deployed on EC2 instances behind a classic ELB. The application uses cookie-based sessions with SameSite=None for cross-origin admin panel access. The IAM role attached to the EC2 instance profile (arn:aws:iam::112233445566:role/AppServerRole) has full IAM permissions (iam:*) to manage user policies and roles. No permission boundaries are applied to the application's IAM role or to target IAM users. The admin panel is served from admin.example.com while the main app is on app.example.com, necessitating the SameSite=None cookie configuration.
